Amphotericin B

Amphotericin B - Clinical Uses

The drug of choice for:

■ Cryptococcal meningitis

■ Mucormycosis (zygomycosis)

■ Invasive fungal infection, not responding to other therapy

Mucormycosis:

  • DOC intravenous Liposomal amphotericin B (5 mg/kg with higher doses possibly given for CNS disease) should be started early
  • Amphotericin B is active against wide range of yeasts and fungi—Candida albicans, Histoplasma capsulatum, Cryptococcus neoformans, Blastomyces dermatitidis, Coccidioides immitis, Torulopsis, Rhodotorula, Aspergillus, Sporothrix, etc.
  • AMB is also active on various species of Leishmania, a protozoa

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions is caused by amphotericin B?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hypokalemia

Hypokalemia Low potassium is not always related to an underlying condition. It may be caused by:

  • Vomiting, chronic diarrhea, or both
  • Certain medications
  • Excessive sweating
  • Under eating or malnutrition

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman with HIV comes to the physician because of an 8-day history of severe pain while swallowing. She has been hospitalized several times with opportunistic infections and has poor adherence to her antiretroviral drug regimen. Endoscopy shows extensive, white, plaque-like lesions in the proximal esophagus. The culture of a biopsy specimen grows Candida albicans. Treatment with intravenous anidulafungin is initiated. Which of the following is the primary mechanism of action of this drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Decreased glucan synthesis.
